You can use simple rules like p { font-size: 1.5rem; }. They won’t affect other elements outside this brick. CSS rules nested in @media and @supports are supported as well.

locale.name: brick.panel.category.customJS.hint

locale.name: brick.control.pdfView.sheetsNumber.description
locale.en:
Specifies the number of pages (sheets) in the selected PDF. The front end displays the corresponding number of boxes, each representing one page.
This setting ensures that the HTML structure with the correct number of boxes is already in place before the PDF file is loaded. This improves loading time (page speed) and prevents layout shifts (CLS), as the display remains stable from the outset.

locale.name: brick.control.pdfView.aspectRatio.description
locale.en:
Reserves space in the front end before loading the PDF file based on the specified aspect ratio.
Please provide a valid CSS value for the aspect-ratio property in the format NUMBER/NUMBER. The default value corresponds to the aspect ratio of an A4 page (210/297).

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step1_1.Text
locale.en:
Welcome to the Block Tour.

Finished bricks are used in template zones. These may differ from template to template.

Take the time to briefly study the following picture. It shows the names of the individual zones. With a click on it the picture can be enlarged.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step2.Text
locale.en:
First we will create our own brick.
The menu for the management of bricks can be found under Administration

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step4.Text
locale.en:
Welcome to the bricks control panel.
Here you can manage your bricks by means of a list.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step5.Text
locale.en: Click Add brick to create a brick.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step6.Text
locale.en: As you can see, a pop-up has opened asking you to select Title and Type of the brick...

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step7.Text
locale.en:
Select from the list e.g. the Brick:
Simple contact form ...

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step8.Text
locale.en: Now select a catchy title for this brick

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step9.Text
locale.en: Click Accept to confirm your entries.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step10.Text
locale.en: Finally, you are automatically navigated to the control panel of the newly created brick.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step11.Text
locale.en:
Under the menu item Information you will find:
  • again the information about the Title of the brick
  • the possibility to store a Description
  • and a note of which Block type the brick is

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step12_1.Text
locale.en:
Under the menu item Properties you can define:
  • Which Areas should be able to include the brick
  • Which settings can be changed by users of the Content Management System (CMS)

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step12_3.Text
locale.en: The brick areas popup gives you an overview of all available brick areas. Press and hold the CTRL key to make multiple selections.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step12_4.Text
locale.en: However, for this example we select Footer brick area ...

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step13.Text
locale.en:
The Settings are brick-specific. This means that different settings are available depending on the brick type. These include among others:
  • the title
  • the size of the brick determine height and width
  • special CSS add classes (especially powerful in connection with Custom CSS)
  • for Google Maps brick: for example, settings for street postcode and city and zoom are added.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step14.Text
locale.en: A WYSIWYG editor can be found under the Content menu item to design the contents of this brick.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step15.Text
locale.en: Don't forget to finally save your settings...

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step16.Text
locale.en: ... and then close the editing interface for this brick.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step17.Text
locale.en:
Now we can insert our contact form into the defined zones of a website.
We go to the start page of your standard project (Main-Project).

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step17_2.Text
locale.en: By the way, you can add these blocks to any of your project pages

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step18.Text
locale.en: .. und Bestätigen die Änderung mit Übernehmen select the menu item Bricks.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step18_2.Text
locale.en: This menu allows you to integrate different bricks in the positions shown graphically on the right.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step19.Text
locale.en: To add the created contact form to the footer of the start page, please click here.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step20.Text
locale.en: Please select your contact form here by clicking on it.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step21.Text
locale.en: Then we can edit the Inheritance settings of the brick.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step22.Text
locale.en:
If you check this box, all children of this page will inherit this brick in the footer.
In this case these are all pages of the project, because pages of the project are subpages of the home page.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step24.Text
locale.en: Here you can remove the brick from the page.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step25.Text
locale.en: You can use the Preview function to see what's changed on your page.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step26.Text
locale.en:
Do you like the implementation of your brick?
Then don't forget to save the changes.

locale.name: tour.general.bricks.Step26.Text
locale.en:
Congratulations.
You have successfully completed the Brick Tour

locale.name: bricks.customerReviewsFlow.description
locale.en:
This brick displays customer reviews in automatically scrolling rows. The entries move continuously like a modern review flow and are especially useful for homepages, landing pages, or trust sections.

  • Multiple rows: Configure one or more rows that are filled with reviews automatically.
  • Automatic movement: Reviews keep moving continuously without click interaction.
  • Flexible direction: All rows can move in the same direction or alternate row by row.
  • Custom reviews: Maintain image, name, addition, link title, link, and review text directly in the brick.
  • Fine-grained control: Adjust speed, spacing for desktop/mobile, and hover behavior.
  • Ideal for social proof: Perfect for showing feedback, testimonials, or community voices in a compact and dynamic way.

This brick is based on automatically scrolling rows and not on a classic slider with arrows or dots.

locale.name: brick.multiLayout.description
locale.en:
This brick gives you the freedom to build page sections around your content instead of forcing your content into a rigid structure. Combine text, images, buttons and other bricks inside a flexible grid that adapts to your layout needs.

Whether you need a compact teaser, a spacious content section or a modular area with multiple focal points, MultiLayout gives you the right foundation. That makes it easy to create individual layouts without being locked into fixed patterns.

  • Flexible layout presets: Start with a preset and adapt the arrangement to your content.
  • Freely assignable areas: Each area can be filled with text, images, buttons or other bricks.
  • Supports sublayouts: If needed, individual areas can contain additional layout structures for even more granular content arrangements.
  • Responsive control: Build the structure for desktop, tablet and mobile exactly as needed.
  • Custom mobile order: Decide in which order content appears on smaller devices.
  • Versatile styling options: Alignment, background image, overlay, colors and spacing can be configured per area.
  • Useful for many scenarios: Ideal for teaser zones, image-text combinations, bento layouts and modular content sections.

That allows you to create everything from simple highlights to complex page sections with a single brick. And you can do it directly in the editor without writing code yourself.

locale.name: brick.multiLayout.gridGap.desc
locale.en: Controls the free space between tiles. Smaller values feel more compact, larger values create more breathing room. The presets are responsive and adapt to the available width: No spacing = 0, Small = subtle, Normal = balanced, Large = airy, Extra large = very airy.

locale.name: brick.multiLayout.tileMinHeight.desc
locale.en: Defines the minimum height of each tile. This helps tiles look calmer and more even when their content lengths differ. No minimum height follows the content only, while Manual allows a custom CSS value such as 240px, 18rem or 30vh.

locale.name: brick.buttons.description
locale.en:
Use this brick to create a list of buttons – e.g. for downloads, contact links or important actions. You can style and link each button individually.

Display mode

  • Button: text (optionally with an icon).
  • Icon only: only icon buttons are shown (entries without an icon are hidden automatically).

Configurable per button

  • Text: the label.
  • Icon: optional symbol (if your site uses an icon set, e.g. Font Awesome).
  • Icon position: icon before or after the text.
  • Button style: e.g. primary/secondary, success/warning (depends on your theme).
  • Size: default, small or large.
  • Link: internal page or external address.
  • Open in new tab: opens the link in a new tab/window.
  • Tooltip (Title): short hint shown on hover.
  • Accessibility (ARIA label): useful for icon-only buttons so screen readers can announce the purpose.
  • Disabled: shown but not clickable.
  • Full width: button uses the full available width.
  • Action on click: optional (advanced) to trigger a function.
  • Additional CSS class: optional (advanced) for custom styling.
  • Hide entry: the button is not rendered at all.

locale.name: brick.button.description
locale.en:
A single button that you fully style and link through its settings. Unlike the "Buttons" brick, display mode and size are set per button.

Configurable

  • Display mode: button, icon only or icon only (rounded).
  • Text and icon: label, optional symbol and its position.
  • Style and size: e.g. primary/secondary as well as default, small or large.
  • Target: internal page or external link – or open a brick in a popup.

locale.name: quiqqer.bricks.buttons.settings.createPopup.identifierDesc
locale.en:
Rendered in the frontend as data-identifier and can be used, for example, for Matomo tracking.
Example: data-identifier="MY_VALUE"

locale.name: quiqqer.bricks.buttons.settings.createPopup.dataAttributesDesc
locale.en: Additional data-* attributes for the button, for example for tracking. The data- prefix is added automatically and spaces become hyphens. Reserved names such as data-qui, data-name and data-identifier are ignored.

locale.name: quiqqer.bricks.buttons.settings.createPopup.brickParamsDesc
locale.en: Values handed to the brick opened in the popup – unlike the button attributes above, which stay on the button itself. Whether a brick evaluates a value is up to that brick. Example: context with the value Package: Starter · Variant: Buy.

locale.name: quiqqer.bricks.buttons.settings.createPopup.openBrick.desc
locale.en: If a brick is selected, it will open in the frontend in a modal window. In this case, the "Link" option is ignored.

locale.name: quiqqer.bricks.buttons.settings.createPopup.openBrick.spacingDesc
locale.en: Enabled by default. Disable it when the brick handles the popup's inner spacing itself (for example edge-to-edge content).
